diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment. The issue is likely due to the new database connection pool configuration in the checkout-api v4.17 release.
diagnosis.root_cause: The checkout-api v4.17 release reduced the database connection pool size to 10 and set the acquire timeout to 2000 ms, leading to connection pool exhaustion and increased latency.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool configuration and set max_connections to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms to 2000.
Staging environment with the same version has a p95 latency of 180 ms, indicating the issue is environment-specific.
Production database connection pool has a high acquire_wait_p95_ms of 1800 ms, indicating long wait times for connections.
All pods for checkout-api v4.17 are running and healthy, ruling out pod-level issues.
The migration to orders-client v3 removed explicit database pool settings, which may have caused the issue.
Staging environment with the same version does not show latency issues, indicating the problem is specific to production.

ruled_out: The staging environment with the same version does not show latency issues, ruling out a general code issue.
All pods for checkout-api v4.17 are running and healthy, ruling out pod-level issues.

proposal.rationale: The checkout-api v4.17 release introduced a database connection pool configuration that caused connection pool exhaustion and increased latency. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, will restore the previous configuration and resolve the latency issue. This is the safest remediation as it reverts the problematic release without affecting other services or environments.
